spec_match.rationale: Measures the cost claim behind the feature's shipping motivation — percent-encoding inflation and URL-construction/load timings for the two schemes — honestly, on real Blob/encodeURIComponent/Image operations, and explicitly defers the taint contract itself to the sibling taint-matrix page.

interactive.rationale: Content-size and run-count sliders update live labels, and Run performs real timed URL constructions and image loads, filling the averaged table, byte bars, and a conclusion drawn from the measured numbers.

blurb_alignment.rationale: The index card frames it as measuring rather than assuming whether the data URI is slower, at sizes from a label to a full page — matching the 5-to-600-row slider and the page's willingness to report the data URI as faster.

edge_cases.rationale: The copy handles noise (averaging, sub-millisecond caveat) and the conclusion branches honestly on whichever path measured faster, but a rejected image load inside the async click handler is uncaught — the button would stay disabled and the output stuck at 'Measuring…' forever.

conformance.rationale: The feature suite proves the readback/export contract this cost story depends on; on Chromium 141 the embedded 'What this browser supports' panel and the /conformance/ route both ran it at 4 pass / 2 fail, the expected pre-156 split.

runtime_evidence.rationale: Headless Chromium 141 (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp): desktop and true-360 mobile screenshots read, DOM dumped, console clean ('[foreignobject-taint:cost] ready'), and the embedded support panel rendered live results — but the Run measurement is click-driven and could not be exercised headlessly, so table and bars stayed at 'Not run yet.' in captures and the measurement path is judged from wiring.

telemetry_health.rationale: showcaseTelemetry?.assert reports 'cost-measured' with row count, byte sizes and inflation after each run, and the load produces no console or network errors; the failure path emits nothing, which matters only if the uncaught-rejection question above is fixed.

design_system.rationale: Everything uses design-system variables, the disabled button state is styled, bars use a translucent accent-blue fill with black mono text on light backgrounds, and there is no static-card pattern or contrast failure.

accessibility.rationale: Both sliders are native ranges inside labels with live value spans, the results table has a caption and proper th scoping including row headers, byte bars carry visible text values rather than colour-only encoding, and the conclusion lands in an aria-live=polite output.

mobile_desktop_parity.rationale: Verified at true 360px and 1280px: controls stack cleanly, the six-column results table compresses without page-level horizontal overflow, and sliders/buttons meet 44px targets on both classes.

openQuestions.title: Uncaught load failure permanently disables the Run button
openQuestions.detail: The async click handler awaits load(dataUrl)/load(blobUrl) with no try/catch; load() rejects on image error, so a failed load leaves an unhandled promise rejection, the button disabled (it is only re-enabled at the end of the happy path), and the output stuck on 'Measuring…' with no retry. Wrap the measurement in try/catch/finally, re-enable the button in finally, and surface the failure in the detail output — the anti-regression list's broken-cancellation/init-race family.

openQuestions.title: The memory claim is asserted, not measured
openQuestions.detail: The lede and conclusion state the inflated data-URI string 'is held in memory alongside the source'. The size table demonstrates inflation but nothing observes retention. Where performance.measureUserAgentSpecificMemory or a simple demonstration (e.g. holding N data URIs vs N revoked blob URLs) is feasible, a small optional probe would move this from narration to measurement; otherwise label it explicitly as background rather than a measured result.

summary: An unusually honest benchmark page: it measures URL-construction and image-load costs for data: vs blob: on the visitor's machine and its conclusion logic is written to report whichever direction the numbers actually show, including the counter-intuitive data-URI-faster case, while presenting the size inflation as the structural difference. Verified with headless Chromium 141 at http://localhost:3000/v156/svg-foreignobject-does-not-taint-the-canvas-for-blob-urls/blob-vs-data-cost/ (cloud, no chrome-devtools-mcp; desktop + true-360 mobile screenshots, DOM dump, clean console; embedded support panel and feature /conformance/ route at 4 pass / 2 fail, the expected pre-156 split). The Run measurement itself is click-driven and was judged from wiring, which is where the one substantive defect sits: a failed image load inside the async handler is uncaught and would leave the button disabled with the UI stuck at 'Measuring…'.
